title: Made a Tesla Roadster flying car browser game in about a day with AI, some notes from the build
author: Parking-Mention-2402
selftext:
Tesla showed the new Roadster this week and I wanted to see how fast I could turn the hype into a playable game. Ended up with a small 3D browser game: you launch off a vertical ramp, land in a night city, and fly over traffic jams with air thrusters. Eat 5 Elon heads, reach the launch pad at 3 km, go to Mars. Ranking is a pure time attack.
    
    Stack is three.js + TypeScript on Cloudflare Workers with D1 for the leaderboard. No assets bought, everything is code: the cars are lofted from cross sections, textures are drawn on canvas, sound is Web Audio synth. Almost all of the code was written with Claude Code while I steered and playtested on my phone.
    
    A few things that surprised me:
    
    - Balancing went way better once I had the AI write headless bots (idle / steer only / perfect play) and run them after every change. First version let an idle player survive 8 minutes because crashed cars cleared the jam for you.
    
    - There was a black flickering on one scene that I could not explain. Turned out a couple of zero-area triangles had (0,0,0) normals, which became NaN in the shader, and the bloom pass smeared that into black blocks.
    
    - After launch everyone at the top had exactly 74.3s. The speed cap made that the mathematical floor, so the leaderboard was just "who got there first". Added a turbo when you eat a head, now the floor depends on how many risky heads you go for (around 65s if you get all 10).
    
    - Google Ads rejected nothing yet, but I kept Elon's face and the Tesla name out of the ad creatives since that is basically asking to get flagged.
    
    It's free, no install, works on phones (portrait only): https://roadster.ubd.gg
    
    Would love feedback on the difficulty curve. Most people die at the first jam, which might be too early. Current record is 66-ish seconds if anyone wants to try.
